title: node-worker
description: A standalone TypeScript worker for BullMQ jobs and Temporal workflows, sharing the API's database.
sidebar:

import { CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A TypeScript process for background work that shouldn't share a process with
the HTTP server: scrapers, schedulers, long-running imports, anything slow or
heavy. It consumes the same Redis queues your API produces to and reads and
writes the same database through Prisma.

```sh
stack new node-worker ./worker --name shop-worker
```

**Stack:** Node 24, TypeScript (ESM, strict), BullMQ, Prisma 7 with the
`pg` adapter, pino, PM2, Docker. Optional: Temporal workflows, Puppeteer.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Entry point | `src/index.ts`, with `src/instrumentation.ts` preloaded through `node --import` |
| Queues | One example consumer on the `example` queue (`src/workers/`) |
| Database | The API's schema, copied or shared as a submodule; this worker owns no migrations |
| Telemetry | OpenTelemetry to OpenObserve: job spans, Prisma and Redis spans, logs, metrics |
| Temporal | `--with temporal`: a worker on task queue `main` with an example workflow and activity |
| Runs as | `yarn start`, PM2 (`ecosystem.config.cjs`), or the Docker image |

## Pairs with

A worker is never alone: it needs the API's **Redis** (to receive jobs) and
**database** (to act on them), and with Temporal, the API's **Temporal
server**. Their settings must match exactly, and a mismatch is silent: the
worker starts, connects, and never receives anything. See [A full-stack
project](../../guides/full-stack/).
